query: How is it different from Java?
answer: The biggest difference is typing. Java is statically typed, so you declare each variable's type and the compiler checks it before the program runs. Python is dynamically typed, so types are worked out at runtime. That means Java catches many mistakes at compile time, while in Python they may only show up when the code runs [1][2]. Java was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems and released in 1996. It was designed to be almost entirely object-oriented, so all code lives inside classes [1]. Python is more flexible: you can write plain scripts, functions or classes, and its syntax is shorter and easier to read. Both run on virtual machines. Java compiles to bytecode for the Java Virtual Machine, which uses just-in-time (JIT) compilation to turn frequently run code into fast machine code. That's the idea behind "write once, run anywhere." The standard Python interpreter, CPython, also uses bytecode, but mostly interprets it. So Java is usually faster, while Python is typically quicker to write [1][2]. In practice, Java is common in large enterprise systems and Android apps, and Python dominates scripting, data science and machine learning.
